answer:
**Drift describes which part of the data distribution changed.** Covariate shift concerns input distribution P(X). Label/prior shift concerns class prevalence P(Y), with additional assumptions often made about class-conditional inputs. Concept drift concerns the relationship P(Y|X). These labels guide diagnosis but real changes can affect several parts at once. [1](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/stats.html)

**Examples distinguish them.** A camera upgrade changes image brightness even if the classification rule is unchanged. A fraud wave changes event prevalence. A new fraud tactic changes what a familiar feature pattern means. A test that detects changed input histograms cannot by itself tell which of these happened.

KS tests compare one-dimensional distributions under their assumptions. PSI and Jensen–Shannon summaries depend on binning or distribution estimates. MMD compares distributions through a kernel and can capture multivariate differences missed by separate marginals. Large samples can make tiny irrelevant changes statistically significant.

**Connect detection to impact.** Monitor missingness, schema validity, feature distributions, prediction distributions, and delayed labeled performance. A change in P(X) may be harmless; an unchanged P(X) can coexist with changed labels or conditional relationships. Investigate critical slices and the operational cause.

Set baselines, thresholds, and response policies using historical variation and practical consequences. A drift alert should trigger diagnosis, not automatically retrain and deploy a model on potentially corrupted data.

**Technical details and references.**

Covariate shift changes $P(X)$ while assuming $P(Y\mid X)$ stays fixed. Label shift changes $P(Y)$ while assuming $P(X\mid Y)$ stays fixed. Concept drift changes the predictive relationship $P(Y\mid X)$. Real deployments can exhibit mixtures. [1](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/stats.html) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

KS compares one-dimensional empirical distributions; PSI summarizes binned proportion changes but has no universal alarm threshold; Jensen–Shannon divergence compares distributions; MMD uses a kernel to detect multivariate discrepancies. Multiple features and repeated checks require calibrated alerting.

Unlabeled feature drift does not prove accuracy degradation, and concept drift can occur without a large marginal feature change. Monitor data quality, prediction distributions, delayed labels, calibration, and business outcomes. Diagnose a shift before retraining: an upstream schema bug should be repaired rather than learned.
